notes: EARNINGS, on the v2 plate kit. The print against what was expected, what
moved, and what it means — in the vertical set only.
There is no stamp. A verdict card is a CALL, and the register is
anti-Cramer by construction: he describes and the viewer decides. What
was a stamp is the closing plate's own line now.

A STATIC PLATE MAY HOLD. The ceiling was written when every plate in the kit boiled; some are `playback: static` now, because a figure that moves is a figure being re-read. What keeps a data beat short is the ceiling itself (`short_max_hold_s`, 8 s), which is already more than a fifty-second cut of eight or nine beats gives any one of them.

ALTERNATE ORDERS CAME BACK WITH THE BEAT MARKERS (items 2 and 26). `sign-off-first` put the closing card ahead of the hook and stays retired: the first second is the ticker and the move. The orders below may move anchored beats, because a marked script says where each beat starts and the cut follows its markers; an unmarked script is only offered the orders that keep the beat sequence it was written to.

WIPES MARK A CHANGE OF SUBJECT (item 13): a shot with `enter: wipe` is wiped in, sweep and page alternating, at most three a short; every other cut stays hard. A wipe on every cut would be a signpost on every cut, which is none.
THE CLEAR AREA (item 27): as the stock short's, every card's words are kept inside the band a phone shows clear of YouTube's own furniture.

THE QUARTER IS ON SCREEN (item 3). The Quarters sheet reached the prompt and the fact-check and never the frame; an earnings short now draws the eight quarters, the three lines against a year before and one row at both horizons from it, and the print against the analysts' average from its consensus rows.

shots.notes: The hook card, second treatment — earnings is not the daily short and should not open on the same picture. THE TICKER AND THE MOVE IN FRAME ONE (item 6): `move` takes the day's signed move and counts up over the first half second while the hook is spoken; `sub` takes the rest of the summary. A summary that does not lead with a signed move leaves `move` empty and keeps the whole summary in `sub`.

alts.notes: The fifth treatment: the hook on a full field with the ticker at the foot, so the eye lands on the sentence before the chip. The same slots. `hook-card-t4` is not here on purpose — it leads with the figure at 240pt, and the next beat is that figure.

shots.notes: A REAL PICTURE (item 34). Every frame of a short was drawn type on the dark ground; this is the company itself, a photograph of its stores or its building off the same chain the long searches (cache, Wikimedia Commons, the company's site), in design's media frame. With no picture found the shot is dropped: a frame round "imagery unavailable" is not a picture. The credit goes out with the video's other credits.
The number that printed, at the size it deserves.

alts.notes: The same figure with a detail rule under it, for a print that has a verdict to carry.

shots.notes: Print against consensus, stacked, each under its own word, as the before-after alternate does. The sheet's first row is not what printed, so it does not label the print. The delta slot stays empty: the gap is a figure nobody wrote, and the pipeline does not compute one.

alts.notes: Print and consensus side by side rather than stacked. Same slot names, so the binds carry; `detail-1` and `detail-2` go unfilled.

What was expected over what came out, as two stacked panels. `body-1` is bound REQUIRED on purpose: the plate's caution is that without a real prior expectation it reads as a comparison against a number it invented, so the rotation only reaches for it when the script carries the consensus. The gap on the divider stays empty — it is a figure nobody wrote, and the pipeline does not compute one.

THE PRINT AGAINST THE STREET, AS ONE GAP (item 3): the Quarters sheet's street-basis actual against its consensus mean, and the beat or miss between them, so the viewer is not left to subtract two big numbers. EPS unless the script's print is an amount, then revenue. Taken whenever the workbook has the consensus rows.

shots.notes: EIGHT QUARTERS OF REVENUE (item 3), off the Quarters sheet, the latest picked out: what the quarter looks like next to the seven before it, which is the question an earnings short is asking.

alts.notes: Revenue, gross margin and EPS against the same quarter a year before: three rows at 52 px, the one table a phone can read.
The quarter's revenue against the quarter before and the same quarter a year earlier. A seasonal December reads as growth on the first and flat on the second, which is the point of showing both.

shots.notes: ONE METRIC A CARD (item 26), as the stock short's numbers: each row a card of its own, its figures the workbook's History sheet (item 23).

alts.notes: Where the row started against where it is, and how far it went: points for a margin, nothing across zero.
The latest figure at display size, with where it came from under it.

shots.notes: What they said about next year, in the card drawn for a term and its meaning.

alts.notes: Guidance as a line worth pulling out rather than a term and its meaning.

shots.notes: The line the print actually means, told to camera in close-up.

meme.notes: The one place for a meme: the tail of the verdict, once both sides of it are on screen and before the close.

alts.notes: The two-sided beat as said-against-happened. Names its slots nothing like `both-true`, so it restates the binds; `wrong` and the three labels are the kit's own and take no binding.

shots.notes: ONE THING AT STATEMENT SIZE, FIRST (item 25). The three-line close drew a conclusion in `line-1` and two empty rules under it, which is the empty furniture the samples were full of. It is an alternate now, and only for a conclusion of exactly three sentences, one a line. The handle sits in the kicker: this plate's date label is in the caption band.

alts.notes: The conclusion as a pulled line.
THREE LINES FOR THREE SENTENCES. `sent.3.i` is sentence i of a conclusion that has exactly three, and nothing otherwise, so this drawing is only in the rotation when every line has one.

orders.name: guidance-first
orders.notes: The guide is the news on some prints and the quarter is the footnote: guidance straight after the hook, then the print against the estimate. Cut only for a script whose markers put `guidance` second.

orders.name: turn-early
orders.notes: The pivot before the years: Dennis says what the beat does not tell you, then the sheet proves it. Cut only for a script marked in this order.
